public_rationale: YipitData's October 27, 2026 release reported Anthropic business-customer retention of 87% after month 12 and 95% after month 24 [e1]. These figures show continued purchasing among sampled business customers, but do not establish that their prices covered actual provider costs or that they represent AI users generally [e1]. They therefore do not settle whether a majority would refuse cost-covering prices or meet the early-resolution rule [e1].
limitations: The release gives no separate measurement endpoint for the quoted retention figures [e1].
The quoted business-retention figures do not represent the full population, including prior free users, and are not matched to verified provider costs [e1].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The majority of AI users will refuse to pay the actual cost of AI.

statement.excerpt: that the majority of users will refuse to pay the actual cost of AI.

our_interpretation: Majority means more than half of users, counted as users rather than weighted by spending.
The ordinary reading concerns existing users faced with prices sufficient to cover providers' actual costs.
The population includes users generally, not only current paying subscribers or enterprise purchasers.
Actual cost requires a disclosed allocation of service-delivery and other relevant costs; API list prices cannot be assumed to equal cost.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence shows that more than half of the relevant users refuse continued purchase when offered comparable AI service at verified cost-covering prices.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence shows that at least half accept and continue paying verified cost-covering prices under comparable service conditions.

evidence.explanation: Observed retention shows substantial willingness to keep buying among sampled business customers. It does not identify prices as cost-covering or represent the full population, so it cannot settle the forecast.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A completed representative transition or field experiment offering comparable service at independently verified cost-covering prices, including prior free users. Observed purchasing decisions over a defined follow-up period must distinguish whether more than half refuse or at least half continue paying.
